title: Ordinary cochain pullback evaluation respects quotient restriction
statement: For a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l, every scheme map f:X→Y, n≥0, strict coefficient-system cochain complex P on Y, and ordinary scalar/direct-image comparison r0 heterogeneously equal to the inverse canonical identity-on-sections comparison, the actual horizontal transition on the inverse-image complex followed by restriction of its level-n evaluation comparison equals its level-(n+1) evaluation comparison followed by finite intrinsic pullback of the transition and the ordinary inverse adjunction mate of r0.inv. The comparison is integralPullEvaluationComplex, explicitly the inverse of pullbackTensorInverseEvaluationComplex followed by the cochain image of pullbackTensorLevelIntrinsic. No localization, derived direct image, K-injective condition or input normalization occurs.

source.place: Construction 4.1, printed p. 21, and the paragraph preceding Lemma 4.10, printed p. 23. Canonical map identifications are the agent-written specialization of this argument to the fixed sequence-site interfaces.

proof.text: In the abelian module categories, transpose the sectionwise direct-image/evaluation identity. The unit normalization of the intrinsic finite comparison identifies the resulting inverse-image comparison. Quotient restriction and direct image are the identity on underlying sections, so naturality in the horizontal sequence arrow gives the equality of the two pullback composites. The universal property of inverse image and sheafification determines the maps from this unit equation. This works also for n=0 and zero systems.

Apply the ordinary identity to P.X i in every degree. The cochain comparison integralPullEvaluationComplex is exactly the mapped ordinary comparison with the canonical composition reordering maps. HomologicalComplex.hom_ext identifies the resulting cochain maps; all differentials commute by naturality.

proof_origin.place: Construction 4.1 and paragraph preceding Lemma 4.10, with canonical mate and localization-factor calculations.

lean.statement:
theorem integralPullEvaluation_cochainSquare {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (n : ℕ)
    (r₀ : normalizedDVRModuleRes l E X (Nat.le_succ n) ⋙
        proEtaleConstantModuleDirectImage f (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 2)) ≅
      proEtaleConstantModuleDirectImage f (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1)) ⋙
        normalizedDVRModuleRes l E Y (Nat.le_succ n))
    (hr₀ : HEq r₀ (proEtaleCoefficientDirectImageComparison f
      (Padic.coefficientExtensionTransition l E (n + 1))).symm)
    (P : CochainComplex (coefficientSequenceModules l E Y) ℤ) :
    (NatTrans.mapHomologicalComplex
        (coefficientSequenceTransition l E X (Nat.le_succ n)) (.up ℤ)).app
        (((pullbackTensorSequenceInverse l E f).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P) ≫
      ((normalizedDVRModuleRes l E X (Nat.le_succ n)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).map
        ((integralPullEvaluationComplex l E f n).hom.app P) =
    (integralPullEvaluationComplex l E f (n + 1)).hom.app P ≫
      ((sfIntrinsicPullback (finiteCoefficientRing l E (n + 2)) f).mapHomologicalComplex
        (.up ℤ)).map
        ((NatTrans.mapHomologicalComplex
          (coefficientSequenceTransition l E Y (Nat.le_succ n)) (.up ℤ)).app P) ≫
      (NatTrans.mapHomologicalComplex
        ((mateEquiv
            (sfIntrinsicConstantModuleAdjunction f (finiteCoefficientRing l E (n + 1)))
            (sfIntrinsicConstantModuleAdjunction f (finiteCoefficientRing l E (n + 2)))).symm
          (TwoSquare.mk _ _ _ _ r₀.inv)).natTrans (.up ℤ)).app
        (((coefficientSequenceEvaluation l E Y n).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P)
